newsitem.title: USA: Dlr starts softer in US after Sakakibara jawboning.
newsitem.headline: Dlr starts softer in US after Sakakibara jawboning.

text.p: The dollar opened easier after a subdued overnight session dominated by remarks from Japanese Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara, which heightened fears of concerted intervention to bolster the yen.
Dollar/yen was heavy under 126 and mark/yen also slipped overnight after Sakakibara, head of the MOF's international finance bureau, said Japan was in close touch with the U.S. over exchange rates.
"The main mover and shaker was the comments from Sakakibara," said Rick Gomes, managing director of foreign exchange at Republic National Bank of New York.
The dollar opened at 125.77/87 yen, down from 126.11/16 at Tuesday's close and at 1.7245/50 marks down from 1.7275/80.
Sakakibara, speaking to reporters after a speech to currency dealers also reiterated that Japan would take decisive action at an appropriate time.
Joint U.S./Japan alarm about the impact of the recently tumbling yen on bilateral trade balances was also reinforced by comments from Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky shortly after the open.
Barshefsky said the U.S. was concerned about its trade imbalance and did not want to see the gap grow wider.

The dollar fell below 126 yen, after briefly garnering support near that level in Tokyo, in the wake of earlier remarks by Sakakibara to the Finance Committee of the Lower House of Japan's of parliament.

"Present exchange rates clearly deviate from economic fundamentals," Sakakibara said, adding that traders views of the Japanese economy were overly pessimistic and that this was reflected in currency movements.
Mark/yen was also damaged by his remarks in Tokyo and fell back below 73.00 after struggling to reclaim that level in the wake of Tuesday's drop.
Dealers said the dollar seems to have decoupled from the recent gyrations in U.S. financial markets.

"We had a nice relief rally in U.S. asset markets yesterday, not accompanied by a dollar rally, so I think those two things have delinked, said Gomes. The market is kind of sitting on the sidelines with one eye on the Bank of Japan.

The dollar failed to catch much updraft from the near- record 135-point rise in the Dow industrials on Tuesday. The dollar may have also been hurt by a decline in U.S. bond yields following Tuesday's surprisingly tame consumer price report, traders said.
Dollar/mark, meanwhile, is looking somewhat vulnerable after setting a new 37-month high on Tuesday, dealers said.

"We made a new high for the year and we need to close the week above 1.7210/20 marks," said John Nelson, foreign exchange trading manager at ABN-AMRO Bank. "If we don't it's probably not a good technical picture for a continued extension in the dollar, in the short term."

Elsewhere the dollar eased to 1.4655/65 Swiss francs from 1.4658/68 and to Canadian $1.3963/68 from C$1.3965/70. The pound fell to $1.6210/15 from $1.6275/85 and the Australian dollar fell to $0.7719/29 from $0.7725/30.
